sources.entry: Openmeetings - Video conferencing, instant messaging, whiteboard, collaborative document editing and other groupware tools using API functions of the Red5 Streaming Server for Remoting and Streaming. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java

summary.one_liner: Apache OpenMeetings is a Java web application for video conferencing, instant messaging, whiteboard, collaborative document editing and other groupware tools.
summary.what_it_does: The README lists video conferencing, instant messaging, a whiteboard, collaborative document editing and other groupware tools as its features. It states that it uses API functions of a media server (Kurento, referred to as KMS) for remoting and streaming. The README describes building with Maven and running a startup script from an extracted distribution archive. Release notes highlight WebRTC audio/video/screen-sharing in rooms, a HTML5 whiteboard, backup/restore, OAuth and LDAP integration, SIP, and a dark theme. The README also mentions an OpenAPI spec and an admin config area. Details beyond these are not given in the README.
use_cases: hosting online meetings and video conferences
running a self-hosted web conferencing server
collaborative whiteboard sessions with a group
team chat and groupware in one place
how_to_run: Install Apache Maven 3.10.0 or later and Java SE 21
Run: mvn clean install -PallModules in the repository root
Extract apache-openmeetings-x.x.x.tar.gz (or .zip on Windows) from openmeetings-server/target
See the Build Instructions and Installation Guide linked in the README
notable: Built on the Kurento Media Server for WebRTC audio, video and screen-sharing in rooms
Includes an HTML5 whiteboard with document upload and conversion
Supports OAuth, LDAP and SIP integration according to release notes
Has a REST/web service API with an OpenAPI spec
Apache 2.0 licensed, part of the Apache Software Foundation
caveats: Requires Java 21 and a compatible Kurento Media Server (KMS 7.3.0+) to run
Older release notes mention that some versions were not production ready; the README's CI badges are empty
keywords: host meetings on my own server
